bull.b: The 108-qubit fidelity milestone validates Rigetti’s modular chiplet architecture at commercial scale. Demonstrated performance can strengthen credibility with enterprise and government customers, support larger-system development, and improve the company’s competitive position as quantum workloads mature.

Substantial liquidity and government funding provide resources to pursue the hardware roadmap without debt financing. The award is also aligned with key technical bottlenecks, potentially extending development capacity and supporting infrastructure investment through the next several quarters.

Broad cloud availability combined with on-premises systems gives customers multiple ways to access Rigetti hardware. This distribution footprint can expand usage, support software and application development, and create a stronger base for future commercial adoption as system capability improves.

bear.b: Heavy operating and free-cash-flow losses show that the business is not yet self-funding. Continued burn can consume liquidity while Rigetti invests in larger systems, increasing dependence on external funding and making execution of the technology roadmap more financially demanding.

Revenue concentration in milestone-based system deliveries and government programs creates uneven quarterly results and makes growth less predictable. This volatility can complicate planning, delay operating leverage, and leave near-term financial performance dependent on customer acceptance timing.

Reaching larger, commercially useful systems requires simultaneous advances across fidelity, interconnects, cryogenics, readout, and error correction. These dependencies raise execution risk and may defer broad commercial adoption, which management expects to accelerate only closer to quantum advantage.
